contract: Retained delivery/dead-letter records in one table under the state/tenant-isolation floor over a consumer-owned Ecto Repo on PostgreSQL 16: Migration.install/1 installs the readers, a table keyed (tenant, source, message_id) holding the canonical record JSON as text, work_ref, put_at_ms and resolution fields, an open-list index and the forced tenant floor; put/3 stores a validated record once (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, equal canonical bytes and work_ref are duplicate, else conflict, a resolved key is not reopened); resolve/3 sets replayed or discarded once (UPDATE only an open row; duplicate, already_resolved, unknown_record); list/3 pages open records of one source by (put_at_ms, message_id) with an opaque cursor, 1..1000; count/2 per source up to 1,000 sources; purge/3 deletes up to limit (1..1000) records for that tenant resolved strictly before the cutoff, oldest first, never open records. After an unknown purge outcome the same request can delete up to another limit eligible records and reports only its own deletion count; it cannot recover the first result. Shape, then the caller's open transaction, are refused before any query; one transact/3 transaction refuses any isolation level but read committed; fixed error atoms; no payload or dispatch.
limits: The state/tenant-isolation limits apply; the consumer Repo's query telemetry receives the tenant and every parameter (record bytes, work_ref, actor_ref).
No payload storage, replay dispatch, alerting or retention policy beyond purge/3; the host chooses when to purge and supplies every time.

list/3 pages by position: a record put later with an earlier put_at_ms than the cursor is not returned by the remaining pages of that walk; a key purged and put again is a new open record. A resolve identifies its record only by (tenant, source, message_id): a retried unconfirmed resolve after that record was purged and its key put again resolves the new record; retry an unconfirmed resolve before purging that record.

An :unavailable result says nothing about whether the write committed; only put/3 and resolve/3 are safe to retry with the same request until that record is purged (after a purge a retried put stores it again as open and a retried resolve is unknown_record or resolves a new record under the same key).
integration/jobs and its closure are test-only dependencies; the library code does not call them.
Finite listed scenarios on one local PostgreSQL 16, including lock-controlled races; not proofs of isolation, atomicity or ordering.

grounding.claim: Listed scenarios on the worker's own disposable PostgreSQL 16 database behind a fail-closed target guard, DBConnection.ConnectionPool Repos (not the Sandbox), random schemas dropped afterwards, application connections SET ROLE to ELZOO_TEST_APP_ROLE with only the README grants (fails when unset): 1 an integration/jobs Relay over a state/outbox Memory Store re-offers an item after a handle that stores then raises once, stored once, second offer duplicate; 2 conflict on another record or work_ref, duplicate of a resolved key does not reopen it, canonical text bytes; 3 resolve once, duplicate, already_resolved, unknown_record, two concurrent resolves held behind another connection's row lock until both wait in pg_locks commit one; 4 list order and paging across limits, resolved absent, count matches, read_limit over 1,000 sources; 5 verify/3 passes, T1 lists, counts and resolves no T2 record and a direct T2 insert fails with 42501; 6 a caller's open transaction gives in_transaction for every function with no query; 7 malformed records are record through Elzoo.DeadLetter.validate/1; 8 a purge with a discarded reply deletes the oldest two of four eligible records, the identical retry deletes the next two and a further retry returns zero; open, cutoff-equal and other-tenant records survive both batches; a purged key put again with a retried resolve (the stated limit); 9 a Relay over a failing first full page delivers later items with the store and blocks them without it; 10 text, work_ref, limit, time, message_id, 16,384-byte record and NUL bounds, and records with 1,025- and 10,000-digit integers and with escaped and non-ASCII texts listed back unchanged; isolation refusal, unreachable Repo and missing table unavailable; no echoed IDs. Dropping the primary key fails case 1, and decoding the stored record with Jason fails the long-integer case (negative controls). Finite scenarios, not proofs.

PostgreSQL 16 INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING waiting for a concurrent inserter, UPDATE re-evaluating its WHERE on the newest row version under read committed, row locks visible in pg_locks, COLLATE "C" byte order, row-level security and transaction_isolation are upstream server contracts reached through Postgrex 0.22.4.

Ecto SQL 3.14.0 Repo.transact/2, in_transaction?/0, Ecto.Adapters.SQL.query!/4 with log: false, migration execute/1 and the query telemetry event are upstream behavior; DBConnection raises for an unreachable pool.
Pinned Jason encodes an ordered object without white space for the canonical record bytes; its decoder refuses integers of more than 1,024 digits, so the Piece does not decode with it.
The tests attach to the Repo's query event to observe that no query runs inside a caller's transaction.
Elixir String.valid?/1, the utf8 binary pattern, Regex anchors and Base.url_encode64/2 for the text, prefix and cursor rules.
OTP 29.1.2 :json.decode/1 reads the stored canonical record back with integers of any length; process, Task and ETS semantics used by the tests.

The consumer runs the migration as the table owner, connects the application as a non-owner, non-bypass role with the README grants, runs transactions at read committed, calls verify/3 at startup, keeps the original work under its own storage keyed by message_id or work_ref, and does not record the Repo's query telemetry parameters.

telemetry.contract: The Piece emits no events and no logs; its queries pass log: false, and the consumer Repo's query telemetry is unchanged (a limit: it receives the parameters).

config.contract: The store value (repo and prefix) is a construction-time operand; fixed Contract bounds (128-byte texts, 256-byte message_id and work_ref, 16,384-byte records, limits 1..1000, 1,000 sources, times 0..2^63-1); no ambient settings and no hot change.

control.contract: No process or lifecycle; resolve/3 and purge/3 are data operations and the consumer owns the Repo, migrations and roles.
